topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its learning objectives on cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss conventional cancer treatment modalities—namely surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their associated toxicities and drug efflux resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic vulnerabilities and checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic approaches that exploit intrinsic tumor vulnerabilities, including hormone dependencies, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and impaired DNA repair.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and resistance pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine oncogene addiction and small-molecule kinase inhibitors, detailing their molecular mechanisms and pathways of acquired resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the therapeutic application of engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to selectively target cancer cell-surface proteins.

topics.label: Immune surveillance and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the principles of antitumor immune surveillance and clinical strategies to harness T cells via checkpoint inhibitors, BiTEs, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Overarching challenges, mortality trends, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review systemic challenges in cancer therapy, epidemiological trends in mortality, future management paradigms, and clinical trial dilemmas.
